svg.title: The cap from the axis
svg.desc: The end of a rotor seen along its axis, to scale. A gold rim ring at 2,500 m radius encloses concentric rings at 850, 1,355, 1,610, 1,900 m above the ground and a hub ring at 140 m radius, all around a 64 m bore. Dots mark the anchors of the axial ties: 96, 48, 48, 24 on the four tie rings and 24 on the hub ring, 240 in all, with a pitch of 108.0 m on the outer ring. Twenty-four radial ribs run between the rings. A table lists the tie count, load, anchor pitch and section of each ring.
svg.text: Looking along the rotor at one end cap: five rings of tie anchors and the ribs between them.
240 ties per rotor, 2,956 m² of carbon in all
Each runs the rotor’s length, cap to cap. The ring loads
add up to 1,988 GN, the air’s push on one cap.
A spoke, for scale, carries 2 GN in 4 m².
An anchor: where one tie meets its ring.
A rib: 24 of them to the 1,900 m ring,
Rim compression ring at the corner.
Lobes 1 to 5 in alternate shades, rim inward.
Each ring is offset half a pitch from the megaframe’s
angular lines, so no tie runs along a pier or beam.
To scale. Ring labels are heights above the ground; the rim is the ground, 2,500 m from the axis.
